wisdom.title: Morning Wisdom
wisdom.text:
🌅 0600 Morning Wisdom

The discipline of the Word is the armor that keeps your mind sharp and your spirit aligned with Heaven’s will.

📖 Scripture — Psalm 119:97-104

Oh, how I love Your law! It is my meditation all the day.
You, through Your commandments, make me wiser than my enemies; For they are ever with me.
I have more understanding than all my teachers, For Your testimonies are my meditation.
I understand more than the ancients, Because I keep Your precepts.
I have restrained my feet from every evil way, That I may keep Your word.
I have not departed from Your judgments, For You Yourself have taught me.
How sweet are Your words to my taste, Sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Through Your precepts I get understanding; Therefore I hate every false way.

⸻

🧭 Context Summary
The psalmist, a man of deep covenant loyalty, declares an obsessive love for the Torah that surpasses all earthly wisdom. He recognizes that true understanding and moral integrity are not products of human intellect but are gifts received through constant meditation on God’s commands. This passage illustrates the profound peace and discernment that come when a man submits his mind entirely to the authority of Scripture.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a REAL MAN — Meditates on the Law

Brother, in a world that prizes quick answers and shallow opinions, you are called to a higher standard of mental discipline. The psalmist does not merely read the law; he meditates on it day and night, allowing it to shape his very thoughts and desires. This is not passive reading but active warfare against the confusion of the age. By fixing his eyes on the commandment, he gains wisdom that outstrips his enemies and understanding that surpasses even the ancients. You, as a father and a veteran, know that vigilance is the price of peace. Your mind must be as guarded as your perimeter, filled only with what is true, noble, and right.

This meditation is the source of your moral clarity. When the psalmist says his feet are held back from every evil way, he speaks of the practical outcome of a mind saturated in God’s Word. You cannot navigate the complex duties of headship and protection if your moral compass is drifting. The sweetness he finds in God’s precepts is the fuel for your endurance. Just as you rely on your training in the field, you must rely on the training of the Spirit through Scripture to discern right from wrong in your home and community.

Therefore, do not neglect the quiet hours. Let the law of the LORD be your primary instruction manual for life. When you face the pressures of providing for your family or leading your household, remember that your strength comes from a mind aligned with Heaven. The world offers you wisdom that leads to destruction, but the LORD offers a wisdom that leads to life. Hold fast to His precepts, brother, for they are the only foundation that will not crumble when the storms of life break upon your home.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Meditates on the Law
• Set aside thirty minutes each morning before the household wakes to read and meditate on Scripture, treating it as your daily briefing.
• Memorize one verse of the law each week to keep it ready in your heart for moments of temptation or decision.
• Audit your mental diet by removing media or sources that contradict biblical truth and replace them with content that edifies your faith.
• Lead your family in a brief discussion of the day’s text, modeling for your children the value of submitting to God’s authority.

🙏 Prayer
Father, I thank You for the gift of Your Word, which is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. Forgive me for the times I have neglected Your law in favor of the fleeting wisdom of this world. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, grant me a hunger for Your precepts that surpasses my hunger for comfort. Give me the discipline to meditate on Your commandments day and night, that I may walk in wisdom and lead my household with clarity and courage. Protect my mind from the lies of the enemy, and fill me with the sweetness of Your truth. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Sharpen your mind daily on the whetstone of Scripture until your understanding eclipses the wisdom of the ancients.

first.title: First Watch — The Husband's Post
first.text:
🕖 0700 First Watch — The Husband's Post

Brother, as you survey the quiet aftermath of judgment, remember that the Lord’s sovereign hand guides both the fall of kingdoms and the fate of His people.

📖 Scripture — 2 Kings 25:22-26 & Jeremiah 40:7-41:18

Then he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left.
Now when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan the son of Careah, Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
And Gedaliah took an oath before them and their men, and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.”
But it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck and killed Gedaliah, the Jews, as well as the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
And all the people, small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose and went to Egypt; for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
And when all the captains of the armies who were in the fields, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed to him men, women, children, and the poorest of the land who had not been carried away captive to Babylon,
then they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah— Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, took an oath before them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
As for me, I will indeed dwell at Mizpah and serve the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.”
Likewise, when all the Jews who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and who were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan,
then all the Jews returned out of all places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruit in abundance.
Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
and said to him, “Do you certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to murder you?” But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam did not believe them.
Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah in Mizpah, saying, “Let me go, please, and I will kill Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it. Why should he murder you, so that all the Jews who are gathered to you would be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?”
But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, “You shall not do this thing, for you speak falsely concerning Ishmael.”
Now it came to pass in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal family and of the officers of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah. And there they ate bread together in Mizpah.
Then Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men who were with him, arose and struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword, and killed him whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Ishmael also struck down all the Jews who were with him, that is, with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war.
And it happened, on the second day after he had killed Gedaliah, when as yet no one knew it,
that certain men came from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men with their beards shaved and their clothes torn, having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD.
Now Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went along; and it happened as he met them that he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam!”
So it was, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah killed them and cast them into the midst of a pit, he and the men who were with him.
But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us, for we have treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field.” So he desisted and did not kill them among their brethren.
Now the pit into which Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men whom he had slain, because of Gedaliah, was the same one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
Then Ishmael carried away captive all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah, the king’s daughters and all the people who remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive and departed to go over to the Ammonites.
But when Johanan the son of Kareah and all the captains of the forces that were with him heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
they took all the men and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah; and they found him by the great pool that is in Gibeon.
So it was, when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, that they were glad.
Then all the people whom Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah turned around and came back, and went to Johanan the son of Kareah.
But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.
Then Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, took from Mizpah all the rest of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah after he had murdered Gedaliah the son of Ahikam—the mighty men of war and the women and the children and the eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they departed and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, as they went on their way to Egypt,
because of the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had murdered Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor in the land.

⸻

🗺️ Briefing Summary

The narrative shifts from the destruction of Jerusalem to the fragile survival of the remnant in the land of Judah. Gedaliah, appointed as governor, attempts to stabilize the region and encourage the people to submit to Babylonian rule for their safety. However, his efforts are swiftly undermined by the treachery of Ishmael, who assassinates him and forces the remaining people to flee into Egypt, demonstrating how human sin can thwart God’s provisional plans for peace.

⸻

❤️ Reflection for Your Wife — H.A.P.P.Y. Husband — Protecting

Brother, the text presents a stark warning against the folly of trusting in the false peace of a compromised leadership. Gedaliah sought to protect the Jews by urging them to serve the Chaldeans, yet his position was untenable because he lacked the authority to enforce justice against the traitors among them. Ishmael, operating in the shadows, exploited this weakness to destroy the governor and scatter the people once more. This serves as a sobering reminder to you, Adam, that peace without justice and protection is merely a prelude to chaos.

As the head of your household, you are called to be a Gedaliah who discerns truth from deceit, but far more importantly, a protector who ensures the safety of his own. You must not be naive to the dangers that lurk in the spiritual and physical realm. Your wife Maria needs to know that her husband is vigilant, discerning, and ready to defend the covenant order of the home. When you see threats to the spiritual well-being of your family, you must act with decisive authority, not out of anger, but out of a steadfast commitment to preserve the peace that comes from obedience to God.

True protection requires both strength and wisdom. You must guard your home from the Ishmaels of this world—those who would sow discord, lie, or lead your family astray from the truth. This does not mean living in fear, but living in preparedness. It means establishing clear boundaries, speaking truth boldly, and ensuring that your household knows the refuge found only in the Lord. You are the shield for your wife; let your faithfulness be her secure ground.

⸏ Personal Application — Protecting

• Conduct a weekly spiritual review of your home to identify any areas where truth is compromised or where external influences are threatening your family’s faith.
• Establish clear and firm boundaries with extended family or friends who consistently encourage behavior contrary to biblical manhood or godly womanhood.
• Speak directly and gently to Maria about your commitment to her spiritual and physical safety, reinforcing that her peace is secured under your faithful leadership.
• Prepare practically for contingencies in your home, ensuring that you are capable of providing for and defending your family in times of crisis.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom

Father, I thank You for the example of Your sovereignty even in the midst of human failure. Grant me the wisdom of Gedaliah to seek peace, but the courage to reject the false peace that leads to destruction. Help me to be a vigilant protector for my wife and children, discerning the traps of the enemy and standing firm against them. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, give me the strength to lead with integrity and the discernment to guard the covenant of our home from all who would seek to undermine it. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Gird your loins with discernment to identify the fatal treachery hiding behind the mask of appeasement.

second.title: Second Watch — The Father's Charge
second.text:
🕚 1100 Second Watch — The Father's Charge
The Lord’s mercy endures even in the ruins of our greatest failures, calling us to rise and serve in His sovereign plan.

📖 Scripture — 2 Kings 25:27-30 & Jeremiah 52:31-34
Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
He spoke kindly to him, and gave him a more prominent seat than those of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin changed from his prison garments, and he ate bread regularly before the king all the days of his life.
And as for his provisions, there was a regular ration given him by the king, a portion for each day, all the days of his life.
Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a more prominent seat than those of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin changed from his prison garments, and he ate bread regularly before the king all the days of his life.
And as for his provisions, there was a regular ration given him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

⸻

🗺️ Field Notes
The king of Babylon, acting under the hidden hand of the Most High God, grants clemency to the deposed monarch of Judah. This act of royal favor preserves the Davidic line, ensuring that the covenant promises remain intact despite the nation’s exile. The LORD orchestrates history to protect His chosen line, demonstrating that His purposes cannot be thwarted by human rebellion.

⸻

👨‍👧 Reflection for Your Children — F.U.L.F.I.L.L.E.D. Father — Faithful
Brother, look to the faithfulness of the LORD in the midst of ruin. Even when Jehoiachin sat in the dark of a Babylonian prison, the God of Israel was not absent. The LORD remembered His covenant with David, and He raised up a king to show mercy. This is the bedrock of our hope: that the LORD remains faithful when we are not. You must teach your sons that their identity is not found in their current circumstances, but in the unchanging character of their God.

To Gideon, who stands at the threshold of manhood, understand that your father’s role is to point you to the ultimate Father who never abandons His own. To Boaz, who is learning the weight of responsibility, see that mercy is a power that restores dignity. And to little Shiloh, know that you are held in the hands of a God who sees you and provides for you daily, guiding you toward the gentle and modest flourishing of a godly young woman. The LORD’s faithfulness is the ground upon which we build our lives.

As a father, I am called to reflect this faithfulness to you. I will not fail you, just as the LORD did not fail His people. I will provide, I will protect, and I will lead you to the truth. Your mother and I stand as one in this covenant duty, guarding your souls with the vigilance of soldiers and the tenderness of parents. We are your earthly covering, pointing you to the Heavenly Covering who is faithful to the end.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Faithful
• Review your daily provision for Gideon, Boaz, and Shiloh to ensure their physical and spiritual needs are met without fail, including guiding Shiloh toward gentle, modest, and godly womanhood.
• Speak words of affirmation to Boaz regarding his growing maturity, reinforcing his identity as a son of the King.
• Establish a consistent bedtime routine for Shiloh that includes a prayer of gratitude for God’s daily faithfulness, nurturing her gentle and modest spirit as she grows into a godly young woman.
• Examine your own heart for any area where you have relied on your strength rather than the LORD’s provision for the family.

🙏 Prayer from the Wardroom
Father, we thank You for Your steadfast love that endures forever. You raised up Jehoiachin from the pit, and You raise us up from our sin. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, grant me the strength to be a faithful provider and leader for my family. Let my house be a testament to Your covenant loyalty. Keep Gideon, Boaz, and Shiloh in the fold of Your grace. Guide Shiloh in her feminine flourishing, nurturing her gentleness, modesty, and godly womanhood. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: When your life feels imprisoned by the weight of your failures, lift your eyes to the King who remembers His covenant and grants mercy in His appointed time.

third.title: Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand
third.text:
🕒 1500 Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand

The sovereign hand of the LORD turns the hearts of kings to fulfill His ancient promises.

📖 Scripture — 2 Chronicles 36:22-23 & Ezra 1

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,
Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth the LORD God of heaven has given me. And He has commanded me to build Him a house at Jerusalem which is in Judah. Who is among you of all His people? May the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up!
Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,
Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth the LORD God of heaven has given me. And He has commanded me to build Him a house at Jerusalem which is in Judah.
Who is among you of all His people? May his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD God of Israel (He is God), which is in Jerusalem.
And whoever is left in any place where he dwells, let the men of his place help him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, besides the freewill offerings for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.
Then the heads of the fathers’ houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, with all whose spirits God had moved, arose to go up and build the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem.
And all those who were around them encouraged them with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.
King Cyrus also brought out the articles of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and put in the temple of his gods;
and Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.
This is the number of them: thirty gold platters, one thousand silver platters, twenty-nine knives,
thirty gold basins, four hundred and ten silver basins of a similar kind, and one thousand other articles.
All the articles of gold and silver were five thousand four hundred. All these Sheshbazzar took with the captives who were brought from Babylon to Jerusalem.

🛰️ Situation Report
Cyrus, the pagan king of a vast empire, finds his will overturned by the invisible hand of the Most High God. The exiles in Babylon, having endured decades of humiliation, are suddenly granted legal permission to return to their ruined homeland. This is not a shift in military fortune but a direct intervention of divine providence to restore the worship of the true God.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a R.E.S.O.L.U.T.E. Citizen — Trustworthy

Fredericksburg (local)
Brother, look to the stones of Fredericksburg. The city stands upon the Rappahannock, a place where the river has seen the blood of patriots and the prayers of soldiers. Just as Cyrus was stirred to rebuild the temple, God stirs the hearts of men to rebuild what is broken. You are called to be a trustworthy steward of this place, defending the weak and upholding the law with a steady hand. The fog of war may obscure the path, but the foundation of your duty remains clear: serve your neighbor and honor your Creator in the daily grind of local life.

Virginia (state)
The Commonwealth of Virginia holds the memory of men who stood firm in their convictions, even when the world mocked them. God has placed you in this land of history and heritage. To be trustworthy here means to honor the institutions He has ordained: the family, the church, and the civil order. Do not falter in your resolve to lead your household with godly authority. The storms of culture may rage against traditional values, but you stand on the rock of Scripture, unshaken by the winds of compromise.

United States (nation)
The nation you serve was founded on the principle that all men are created by a Sovereign God and owe Him allegiance. Cyrus, though unaware of the truth, served God’s purpose by restoring the Jewish remnant. You, as a citizen and a veteran, serve a higher King. Your trustworthiness is demonstrated in your obedience to just laws and your readiness to defend the liberties that allow the Gospel to flourish. Do not look to the politicians of this age for salvation; look to the Lord, who raises up kings and brings them low according to His holy will.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Trustworthy
• Inspect your home’s defenses and ensure your family is secure in the faith.
• Review your financial commitments to ensure you are honoring God with your resources.
• Speak truth to power in your workplace without fear of man.
• Dedicate time each day to pray for the leadership of the nation and the church.

🙏 Prayer from the Bridge
Father, You are the Sovereign Lord who stirs the hearts of kings and the souls of men. We thank You for Your faithfulness to Your covenant people. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen us to be trustworthy citizens who honor You in our homes, our work, and our service. Give us the courage to stand firm in the truth when others compromise. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Heed the royal decree and pick up your hammer to rebuild what time and temptation have left in ruins.

🦅 This Day in American History — June 13
On June 13, 1786, Winfield Scott was born in Virginia, a soldier who would serve his country faithfully under the flag for more than half a century and command its army through war and peace as the Grand Old Man of the Army. On the same day in 1927, four million New Yorkers lined the streets to shower Charles Lindbergh with a ticker-tape parade, honoring a young airman who had kept faith with a daring promise and flown alone across the Atlantic to Paris. A Trustworthy citizen earns such honor as these men did, by long fidelity to his duty and by making good on what he sets out to do, that others may rely on his word as on a thing tested before God.

peace.title: Evening Peace
peace.text:
🌙 2100 Evening Peace

The day’s labor yields to the quiet watch of God’s faithful keeping.

📖 Scripture — Psalm 147

Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing praises to our God; For it is pleasant, and praise is beautiful.
The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers together the outcasts of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted And binds up their wounds.
He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding is infinite.
The LORD lifts up the humble; He casts the wicked down to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; Sing praises on the harp to our God,
Who covers the heavens with clouds, Who prepares rain for the earth, Who makes grass to grow on the mountains.
He gives to the beast its food, And to the young ravens that cry.
He does not delight in the strength of the horse; He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man.
The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him, In those who hope in His mercy.
Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem! Praise your God, O Zion!
For He has strengthened the bars of your gates; He has blessed your children within you.
He makes peace in your borders, And fills you with the finest wheat.
He sends out His command to the earth; His word runs very swiftly.
He gives snow like wool; He scatters the frost like ashes;
He casts out His hail like morsels; Who can stand before His cold?
He sends out His word and melts them; He causes His wind to blow, and the waters flow.
He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel.
He has not dealt thus with any nation; And as for His judgments, they have not known them. Praise the LORD!

⸻

🌾 Reflection for a Man at Home and in Community

As a HAPPY husband, I see in this text the tender care of the Shepherd who binds up wounds and repairs what is broken. Brother, your home is not merely a shelter but a sanctuary where the Lord’s restorative power flows through your gentle words and steadfast presence. You are called to be the visible sign of Christ’s love, mending the fractures of the day with grace, patience, and a firm but loving authority that points your wife to the One who truly heals.

As a FULFILLED father, I recognize that the Lord counts the stars and knows them by name, just as He knows every detail of your children’s lives. Your duty is to lead them in the fear of the LORD, teaching them that their value is secured by their Creator, not by their performance or strength. You must provide for them not only in material needs but in spiritual direction, ensuring that they learn to fear the LORD and hope in His steadfast love, rather than placing their trust in their own power.

As a RESOLUTE citizen, I acknowledge that the Lord takes no pleasure in the strength of the horse or the legs of a man, but delights in those who fear Him. Your military discipline and civic strength are tools to be surrendered, not idols to be worshipped. You stand ready to serve and protect, yet you rest in the truth that true security comes from the LORD alone, who lifts up the lowly and casts down the proud. Let your service be an act of worship, grounded in humility and dependent on His grace.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom

Father, we thank You for the peace of this evening and the assurance of Your sovereign care. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen us to lead our homes with godly authority and tender love, and to walk as faithful citizens who fear You alone. We surrender our efforts, our strength, and our families into Your hands, trusting that You who numbers the stars numbers our days and cares for our souls. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Tend your flock with the Shepherd’s gentle authority, binding the brokenness of your household through the restorative power of your steadfast presence.
